artifact: independent finite whole deep-life teaching kit
ownership: Five new core meshes, colour maps, tissue materials and bounded poses are original project-authored code. Three.js geometric helpers and BufferGeometryUtils are MIT. No third-party model, photograph, video or texture was downloaded or embedded.
sourceUse: The linked scientific and institutional pages guide identification, anatomical outline, measurement axes and functional behavior. Their images are reference evidence, not copied assets; copyright is not claimed to be a reusable mesh licence.
scope: 700m middle-water and 3500m seafloor representatives in the northeast Pacific. Source ranges overlap but do not establish one surveyed co-occurrence community. Camera descent is time-compressed travel illustration, not an actual measured dive or ocean transect.
unchangedOriginals: all original ecological records and storage namespaces
factsAndDisplayChoices: Taxonomic levels and selected anatomical sizes come unchanged from the existing source catalogs; selected ratios, pigment patterns, appendage sampling, tissue transmission and motions are uncalibrated teaching choices.

The four sea pigs, three rattails and three anemones read one separate in-memory native local model. Only its actual lastFeedAt drives an oral-feeding visual cue; this module never creates intake events or updates food ledgers.
The middle-water animals and three functional additions use bounded display trajectories and have no invented native ingestion, population clock or ecological stock.

Marine snow is a finite camera-local light-scattering display volume; authored prior bed traces and detrital colour patches are scenery, not recorded feeding, carbon mass, or saved environmental history.

At 700m extremely weak natural light may exist but is not calibrated here; visible subjects are illuminated by the observation vehicle. At 3500m there is no sunlight or local photosynthesis. Only one observation spot light casts finite contact shadows.

Ophiosphalma arm span and Thalassocrinus complete height are not independently verified field maxima. The existing catalog retains illustrative span and arm-length axes without promoting them to natural size distributions.
